key_insight: VULCAN combines gradient-free ansatz growth, circuit compression, and perturbative correction to reduce the quantum measurement cost of electronic-structure calculations.
engineering_relevance: Smaller operator pools, controlled circuit depth, and reduced qubit requirements offer a resource-efficient pathway toward quantum chemistry on quantum computers.
method: Generate operators with Variational Double Bracket Flow and append full layers without Hamiltonian-gradient measurements.
Compress grown circuits using state-overlap measurements and project the Hamiltonian onto a dominant-determinant subspace.
Apply GPU-accelerated stochastic Epstein–Nesbet perturbation theory (ENPT2) to recover residual correlation and enable early stopping.
evidence_signal: In emulation up to 32 logical qubits, VULCAN reached chemical accuracy for hydrogen chains, BeH2, and H2O at 5–20% of batched ADAPT-VQE’s measurement cost; one layer plus ENPT2 also reached chemical accuracy for 32-qubit C3H6, where the baseline did not.
watch_item: Results are based on high-performance emulation; noisy-hardware performance and end-to-end costs including compression and classical ENPT2 remain important validation targets.
paper_title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
